div.p: CYVANTAS helps organizations uncover vulnerabilities, understand their real attack surface, and build stronger defenses through offensive security, penetration testing, vulnerability research, and adversarial intelligence.

svg.title: Illustrative model of an organization's attack surface: web, API, cloud, network, mobile, identity and OSINT nodes connected to a central target.

div.h2: A cybersecurity brand built around one question: where are you actually exposed?
div.p: CYVANTAS is an offensive-security-focused cybersecurity organization. We work from the attacker's perspective to give organizations a realistic view of their risk, then translate that view into practical steps toward a stronger security posture.

ul.li: Finding real attack paths, not just isolated issues
Understanding exposure across applications, APIs, cloud and identity
Validating vulnerabilities to remove false positives
Reducing attack surface with concrete remediation steps
Producing actionable security intelligence for engineering teams

div.div: Philosophy“Find it. Understand it. Secure it.”

div.p: Security testing should do more than find weaknesses. It should tell you exactly how to fix them. Every CYVANTAS engagement follows the same process.

li.p: Identify assets, applications, infrastructure and attack surface.
Understand technologies, trust boundaries, exposed services and potential attack paths.
Confirm vulnerabilities and eliminate false positives.
Where authorized, demonstrate realistic impact safely.
Provide actionable remediation guidance and validation.

p.span: Responsible testing: assessments are performed only against systems and assets that are explicitly authorized and in scope. Exploitation is limited to safe, agreed demonstrations of impact.

div.h2: Vulnerabilities live in an interconnected attack surface
div.p: A weakness rarely matters in isolation. What matters is the path an attacker can chain from the internet to something you care about. Hover or focus a layer to trace it.

svg.title: Layered attack-surface diagram from the internet down to third-party dependencies, with cross-links between layers.

div.p: Everything reachable from the outside.
Registered names, DNS records and ownership.
Forgotten, staging and takeover-prone hosts.
Logic, sessions and access control.
Authentication, authorization and data exposure.
Identity policies, storage and network rules.
Exposed services, devices and mobile clients.
Accounts, tokens, SSO and privilege paths.
Vendors, libraries and integrations you inherit.
Findings should be supported by technical evidence — reproducible steps and proof, not scanner output alone.
Don't look at vulnerabilities in isolation. Chained together, small weaknesses become real routes into a system.
Prioritize understanding actual security impact over theoretical severity.
Continuously investigate emerging vulnerabilities and attack techniques.
Security reports should help engineering teams fix problems, with clear priorities and steps.
